- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., 48.25 → 48.03, 49.61 → 49.16), suggesting overshoot bias.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–7 days post-event; adjust for delayed reaction.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and fails to capture mean reversion toward historical averages.
- After a spike, model often holds high prices for 3–5 days before correcting — apply downward correction if price drops below 10% of peak.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overconfidently assumes continuation of recent trend; reduce forecast momentum if no new event triggers.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in early period (first 10 days) and overestimates in late period (last 10 days) — apply smoothing or weighted decay to avoid tail bias.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal (e.g., 49.61 → 35.94), model fails to adjust — apply “reversal trigger” rule: if 3 consecutive days drop >5%, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day until stabilization.
